svg.title: Order pipeline: from a click or an AI decision to the arrival executor
svg.desc: How an order travels: the player's click or the commander AI's $6822 write, the command slot $58016, the executor $6a3a / $6ac6, the three routes (run now, the dead direct branch $6b20, the carrier pigeon $4562), the pigeon's arrival $41dc clearing the pending word at $4220, the handler table $6b5a, the senders and the arrival executors, with the gate that proves each step. Sources: reversing/powermonger/strategy.md "The commander AI `$6522`" (queued orders, "The pending word"), "`$6822`: issuing an order", "`$6a3a` / `$6ac6` / `$6b38` the order executor", "The executor, proven", "What an AI invention order does", "The order senders and arrival executors, proven", "Transfer `$664c`, `$668c`" (k25: pigeon landed 6,279,910 steps later); reversing/powermonger/ai.md "`$4562` how an order reaches a subordinate captain" (routing, the dead direct branch, gate_pigeon_send.py), "The carrier-pigeon pool", "An arrival of another lord's pigeon" ($41dc). $4220 = clr.w -72(A0) inside the $41dc arrival block and $6b20 = clr.w -72(A1) checked by disassembly of scratchpad/pm123/win/m1_map.ram. Full fact list: order_pipeline.facts.md.
svg.text: How an order reaches a unit, and how a stuck "order in flight" flag can freeze an army
Box border = how well each step is verified; the green line in a box says which check verified it. Counts come from the runs or checks named in the box.
proven (checked against the game's own code)
observed (seen in the running game)
inferred (read from the code, not run)
PowerMonger (Bullfrog / Electronic Arts, 1990, here the Atari ST version) is a war game in which you give orders, not controls: the
player picks an order icon (go, attack, get men, take food and so on) and clicks a target on the map, and a captain's group walks there
and acts. The computer lords issue their orders through the same command slots and the same executor. The first captain's own group acts
at once; an order for any other captain is carried to him by a carrier pigeon and takes effect when it lands. This figure comes from
reverse-engineering the game's 68000 machine code (the ST's CPU) and running it in an emulator.
The figure follows one order from the click or the AI's decision to the routine that carries it out, and tracks the pending word
4(group), also called the in-flight flag: the field that marks a group whose order is still in the air, and which the commander AI reads
as "do not decide for this group". If it stays set, the group is frozen; the large blue box shows how that happens.
$ numbers are addresses in the game's memory, given as citations; the text says what each one is. Evidence: proven = checked against the game's own code
with a match count; observed = seen in the running game; inferred = read from the code or reasoned, not run.

The in-flight flag, the pending word 4(group) (base + 4 + 2k = -72 from the group offset)
Set by $6822 for any group but the side's own. Cleared only at $4220 (pigeon
landing) and $6b20. While it is set, the AI loop ($6564) skips the group.
Stuck flags, a game bug after the side's first group dies:
$2776 frees the side's pigeons ($27c6), pending words stay set;
a new $4562 copies the dead sender's owner byte ($45a8), and
$3e06 skips a pigeon with owner <= 0 ($417a): it never flies.
Counted over 183 saved games from live play, 357 set flags: 70 pigeon in flight, 142 dead
sender, 141 no pigeon left, 4 queued; 4 with a live first group.
Dispatch ($6b38): clear the type; types >= $34 exit; otherwise jump through the table at $6b5a by type
proven: handler choice 32/32; observed: 12 dispatches at $6b56 over 6 handlers (one saved game)
Senders (the handlers for each order type)
$4a7a, $1c18: group state, lead target cell, lead mode $10
proven: 61143/61143 bytes over 2273 states;
and 36/36 register sets (wrapper check)
The lead walks ($14b62), then the arrival executor
$3956 (mode $74), $3da4 ($7a), $5fa0 ($22): proven with the senders
AI invention order $0e (observed): handler 157k to 181k steps after $6822
(4 issues); arrival 295k to 525k steps after $6c48 (22 of 22);
26 of 30 natural orders reach $5fa0, 4 replaced by a later order
For the side's own group (D7 = 0) $6822 writes 4(group) := 0. A local $22 reaches $3ce8 only while $2df96 is set. Player order to a second captain, observed in
one saved game: $3ce8 sets $58042[side] := $18a; the posture click launches $4562 (1 hit), counter $57fd8+2 goes 0 to 1, $41dc writes it back to 0
(at $4206) about 9.97M steps later, and $35a0 sets group 1's posture 3 to 2. Steps are emulator instructions.

svg.text: How to read it
Read top to bottom: boxes are the routines an order passes through and arrows the path it takes. Row 1 holds the two sources. $6822 writes an order
for the side's own group (the one $58042 names) straight into the side's command slot ($58016, one 6-byte slot per side); for any other group it
writes the order into the side record's header and sets the in-flight flag (the pending word). Every tick the executor $6a3a reads the slots and
$6ac6 picks one of three routes: run now (left), a direct branch that is dead in play (middle, dashed), or a carrier pigeon (right) that flies for
millions of steps and, on landing, clears the flag and hands the order on. The routes meet at $6b38, which dispatches on the order type to a sender;
the group's lead then walks to the target, where an arrival executor finishes the order. The large blue box is the in-flight flag and its bug.
Takeaway: the commander AI skips a group while its in-flight flag is set, so an order that never lands freezes that group. When a side's first group
dies its pigeons are freed but the flags stay set, and later orders copy the dead sender and never fly: of 357 set flags in 183 saved games from live
play, 142 belonged to a dead sender and 141 had no pigeon.
Terms and evidence
Proven: the routine was rewritten in Python and run beside the game's own 68000 code, called in isolation from saved game states with the emulator's
callcap command (which runs one routine from a saved state and records what it changed), and every changed byte matched; "1567/1567" is matching
bytes out of bytes compared, "125 states" the saved states used. Observed: seen in the running game and counted. Inferred: read from the disassembly
only. Steps are emulated 68000 instructions. 4(group) is the pending word and 76(group) the state, in the AI's frame (side base + 2k for group k);
-72(A0) is the same pending word reached from the group offset. Posture is a group's aggression setting (2 aggressive, 3 neutral, 4 passive).
Sources: strategy.md "The commander AI $6522", "$6822: issuing an order", "The pending word", "The executor, proven", "The order senders and arrival executors, proven", "What an AI
invention order does", "$51538 group-order table" (posture); ai.md "$4562 how an order reaches a subordinate captain"; saved games m1_s0, rand1, rand1_s1 (one side also watched for
150M steps), k25 (land 25), k60_s2; scripts gate_cmdai.py, gate_exec.py, exec_census.py, gate_pigeon_send.py, gate_orders.py, wrapper_check.py, py/arms/pending_census.py,
py/captain2/drive_order.sh; order_pipeline.facts.md.
